Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the parking lot collision
you reported in Katy, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd ratehr just give you the details of what happened, if that's okay.
Q: That's fine, but I do need the name on the record first, and then we can go through the events.
A: Understood. It's the policyholder's driver speaking.
Q: Thank you. Can you walk me through what happened when you pulled into the lot?
A: I was backing out of a space near the store entrance. It was busy, with carts everywhere. I chceked my mirror, saw
nothing, and started to reverse slowly.
Q: What was your speed when the impact occurred?
A: Very slow, maybe walking pace. I felt a bump and stopped right away.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before contact?
A: No. It came from my blind side, behind the SUV parked next to me.
Q: How are you feeling now?
A: Not great. I hit my head on the steering wheel when I braked. I had a headache that got worse, and I felt dizzy and
foggy for a while. My doctor has told me I have a concussion and I need to limit screen time and rest.
Q: Did you seek medical attention the same day?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon, and I was referred for follow-up.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I'll send any medical paperwork you need.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.

  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.

"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
